## Take out the highest common factor

Find the largest factor shared by every term. Divide each term by it to fill the bracket.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$12x^2+18x$

::: {.fragment}

[Both coefficients share 6. Both terms contain $x$.]{.annotation}

Highest common factor: $6x$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Find the two missing factors.]{.annotation}

$6x(2x)=12x^2$ and $6x(3)=18x$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Write the product.]{.annotation}

$12x^2+18x=6x(2x+3)$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$12x^2-18x$

Predict what changes when the second term is negative. Factorise on paper.

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Check your working]{.annotation}

The common factor is $6x$. The second term in the bracket is $-3$.

$12x^2-18x=6x(2x-3)$.

:::
